title: Candle Psychology
hook: Going deeper. What specific candle behavior means for your next read.
mission: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to explain why two similar-looking candles at the same level can tell opposite stories.

blocks.heading: Every candle is a buyer and seller battle

beats.heading: The close shows who held control
beats.body: Buyers push price up. Sellers push price down. The candle close shows who held control by the end of that candle.

beats.heading: Not just green or red
beats.body: I'm not just asking if the candle is green or red. I'm asking where it reacted, where it rejected, and where it closed.

blocks.heading: Same support level, different outcomes
blocks.prompt: Price comes into support, wicks down — see whether it holds or fails by watching the close.

config.caption: Tap "Show the rejection" to see buyers defending the level

blocks.heading: Are they telling the same story?
blocks.scenario: Two candles form at the same support level with nearly identical wicks, but one closes above support and the other closes below it.

options.label: No — one shows buyers defending the level, the other shows sellers actually breaking it
options.feedback: Right — reading only the wick would make two very different events look the same.

options.label: Yes — similar wicks always mean the same outcome
options.feedback: The close is what separates "defended" from "failed."

blocks.quote: I'm not just asking if the candle is green or red. I'm asking where it reacted, where it rejected, and where it closed.

questions.question: What does a candle close help you read?
questions.why: The close is the scoreboard for who actually won that candle.

questions.question: Before calling acceptance above a level, wait for the candle ___.
questions.why: The close is what confirms acceptance, not the wick or the color.

takeaways: Buyers and sellers fight inside every candle — the close shows who won.
Similar wicks can hide opposite outcomes — the close is the tiebreaker.
Read where price reacted, rejected, and closed — not just its color.
remember: It's not green or red. It's where it closed.
